identity_evidence.quote: The patient was a 37-year-old woman who was transferred to our hospital due to an unsuccessful repair of a rectovaginal fistula after hemorrhoid surgery in a local hospital.

attribution_limitations: The reexamination after the continued diversion is described as the inflammation having disappeared in the abstract and results, but as the margin inflammation being significantly relieved with the fistula still visible in the case description.

The interval to the endoscopic reexamination after ileostomy is 8 weeks in the text but the Figure 1E-H caption says 1 month after ileostomy; the text also says the diversion lasted 8 weeks (4 weeks as required).

The 12-week endoscopy is "12 weeks later" than the 5-week reexamination in the body text, but "After 12 weeks of surgery" in the abstract and "3 months after repairing operation" in the Figure 3 caption; the 5-week visit is "1 month" in the caption.
The 7-day treatment combines prophylactic ileostomy, fecal diversion and cephalosporin antibiotic; the antibiotic duration and drug name are not stated separately.
"The infection status of the stoma was serious" does not say whether the stoma is the fistula orifice or the ileostomy (the text calls the fistula orifice a stoma elsewhere).
